articles.title: Public Health Emergency Declared In Karaikal For Acute Diarrhoeal Disease - BW Healthcare World
articles.description: The Directorate of Health and Family Welfare Services of Puducherry on Sunday declared a 'public health emergency' in Karaikal region, an outlying pocket of the Union Territory, following an outbreak of acute diarrhoeal cases over the last few days. A release from the Director of Health G Sriramulu said a large number of people were found to be suffering from acute diarrhoeal disease."A large number of people were affected by the disease," he said, adding that examination of drinking water samples in the region was found to be not good for consumption. Sriramulu said some of the patients reportedly positive for cholera. He said more cases were reported in hospitals daily and special teams of doctors have been formed to take stock of the situation. Steps to manage the situation are being taken in coordination with the Public Works Department and Municipalities, he said. Contamination of drinking water was allegedly the reason for the spread of the disease, he added. People were instructed to drink only boiled water. Hotels and restaurants were also asked to supply only boiled water, the official said. Around 700 people were admitted in the hospitals in Karaikal so far, an official source told PTI.Meanwhile, Puducherry Education Director Rudra Goud said all schools and colleges would remain closed for three days from Monday 'due to outbreak of cholera' in Karaikal region. However, Board examinations for polytechnic colleges would be held as per scheduled, the Director said. Transport Minister Chandra Priyanka, hailing from Karaikal, rushed to the region on Saturday and reviewed the situation. A release from office of the Minister said along with PWD Minister K Lakshminarayanan a detailed review of the situation was made in Karaikal today .Samples of water supplied from an overhead tank in the region were taken to assess the quality of the water, said the release. Local legislator A M H Nazeem, District Collector Mansoor and Director of Health of Puducherry were among those who participated in the review of the situation, it added. Also, Lieutenant Governor Tamilisai Soundararajan held discussions with the officials of Health Department through video-conference from Telangana (of which she is the Governor) and directed the officials to take immediate steps to prevent spread of the disease. She asked the Health Department to ensure supply of ORS packets to the patients to protect them from the impact of the diarrhoeal disease, said a release from office of the Lieutenant Governor.(PTI)

articles.title: Death Toll Rises To 14 In Mysterious Disease Outbreak In Jammu And Kashmir - BW Healthcare World
articles.description: The death toll from a mysterious illness in Badhaal village, located in the remote Koteranka Sub-division of Jammu and Kashmir's Rajouri district, has risen to 14, following the deaths of two more family members, including a six-year-old girl, officials reported on Tuesday. The fatalities, which include 11 children and 3 adults from three families over the past 30 days, have triggered widespread panic among the village residents. The authorities have mobilised health teams to investigate the cause and mitigate potential health risks. As reported by PTI, Safina Kousar, one of the victims, passed away at a hospital in Jammu, where her three siblings had succumbed to the disease over the last two days. Two other siblings remain in critical condition. Additionally, the children's grandfather, Mohd Rafiq, died at a hospital in Rajouri on Monday. According to media reports, last month, nine individuals from two families in the village died, initially leading to suspicions of food poisoning. However, as more villagers exhibited similar symptoms, the authorities escalated the investigation and called in health experts from across the country. Investigations UnderwayDr. Ashutosh Gupta, Principal of Government Medical College Hospital in Jammu, previously suggested that a viral infection could be responsible for the deaths, though further studies were needed to confirm the exact cause. Experts from prestigious institutions, including Pune's National Institute of Virology, PGI Chandigarh, AIIMS Delhi, and the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), Delhi, have been deployed to assist in the ongoing investigations. Government Response and MonitoringRajouri District's Deputy Commissioner, Abhishek Sharma, is personally overseeing the situation to ensure a prompt response. Health teams are conducting extensive contact tracing and collecting samples from the region. Food and water samples have also been gathered to assess the safety of essential supplies. A dedicated Health Department team, led by Jammu Health Director Dr. Rakesh Mangotra and Rajouri Chief Medical Officer Dr. Manohar Rana, has set up operations in Kandi Kotranka to manage the crisis. A mobile medical unit and ambulance are on standby to address urgent medical needs. The district administration has urged the public to cooperate with health officials during the surveillance and intervention efforts. Residents with health concerns are encouraged to contact the district control room or local health authorities for assistance.

articles.title: Hillary Clinton tests positive for COVID-19, Bill Clinton negative but in quarantine
articles.description: WASHINGTON (TND) — Former Secretary of State and Democratic presidential nominee Hillary Clinton has tested positive for coronavirus, she said Tuesday. She wrote on Twitter that she has mild symptoms and is "feeling fine. " Former President Bill Clinton has tested negative and is in quarantine, she said. "I'm more grateful than ever for the protection vaccines can provide against serious illness. Please get vaccinated and boosted if you haven't already! " Hillary Clinton said.

articles.title: Hong Kong reopens beaches and pools, Beijing begins relaxing quarantine rules
articles.description: BEIJING (AP) — Hong Kong reopened beaches and pools on Thursday in a relaxation of COVID-19 restrictions, while China's capital Beijing began easing quarantine rules for arrivals from overseas. Hong Kong had closed water sports venues during an outbreak of the highly transmissible omicron variant, but has been reducing restrictions as cases decline. Deaths from COVID-19 have fallen from a high of almost 300 per day in March to zero in recent days.
